entities.summary: The Vithoba Temple, officially known as Shri Vitthal-Rukmini Mandir is a Hindu temple in Pandharpur, in the Indian state of Maharashtra. It is the main centre of worship for Vithoba, a form of the god Vishnu or Krishna, and his consort Rakhumai. It is one of the 108 Abhimana Kshethram of Vaishnavate tradition. The temple was built by King Vishnuvardhana (Bittideva) of Hoysala Empire between 1108 and 1152 CE upon being convinced by the historical figure Pundalik. Also, there is an inscription in the temple, of a Hoysala King Vira Someshwara dating back to 1237 CE, which grants the temple a village for its upkeep.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: The Vithoba Temple played a significant role in shaping regional Hinduism and Vaishnavate tradition, with its construction by King Vishnuvardhana between 1108 and 1152 CE. The temple's historical significance is also underscored by the inscription of Hoysala King Vira Someshwara dating back to 1237 CE.
